F08-end-truncated-in-member: must reject

An archive that ends inside the data of a member.

The header of `a` says 1024 bytes, but the file ends after 512 of them. Depending on the
implementation, the part it has is extracted, nothing is extracted, or extraction fails. Archives
that are distributed are pinned by their sha256, so this archive is damaged, not ambiguous: it is
rejected all the same.

Decision point: whether a member that is cut short is extracted.
Seen in: no source tarball, where a damaged download fails its sha256.
See also: F04, an archive cut short after a complete member, or one without an end-of-archive
marker, which is rejected as well.

0x000000  header: regular file, size 1024
          name     [  0,100)  "a" + 99 NUL
          mode     [100,108)  "0000644" + NUL  644 (octal)
          uid      [108,116)  "0000000" + NUL  0
          gid      [116,124)  "0000000" + NUL  0
          size     [124,136)  "00000002000" + NUL  1024
          mtime    [136,148)  "00000000000" + NUL  0
          chksum   [148,156)  "007340\0 "  3808: the unsigned sum of the header, this field as spaces
          typeflag [156,157)  "0"  regular file
          linkname [157,257)  100 NUL
          magic    [257,263)  "ustar" + NUL
          version  [263,265)  "00"
          uname    [265,297)  32 NUL
          gname    [297,329)  32 NUL
          devmajor [329,337)  "0000000" + NUL  0
          devminor [337,345)  "0000000" + NUL  0
          prefix   [345,500)  155 NUL
          pad      [500,512)  12 NUL
0x000200  data: the first 512 of the 1024 bytes, and then the file ends
          512 bytes, then 0 NUL
          ""
0x000400  end of file
